steps.what: Select medical dictation and verify report identity and template
Transcribe dictation into the required medical report

loop.purpose: Produce a draft faithful to the selected dictation
loop.input: Verified audio version and report template
loop.output: Draft transcription with audio links and uncertain spans
loop.check: Transcriptionist listens against source audio and checks meaning, omissions, negation, numbers, laterality and terminology; unclear speech is not guessed
loop.stop: One transcription and one correction pass; unusable audio returns to manual transcription or dictator clarification
loop.why_not_simpler: Native dictation recognition is tried first; varied medical speech cannot be handled by fixed field merges

steps.what: Check transcription completeness and hand off the report for clinical sign-off

tasks.design: Configure approved dictation recognition in the clinical documentation system {OTHER} before custom tooling. The transcriptionist corrects the source-linked draft and hands off a checked version; clinical approval remains the dictator's existing responsibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Typing dictated narrative takes time even when the audio is clear.
tasks.enabler_now: Medical speech tools can draft text while source listening and correction remain necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Poor audio, ambiguous words and clinically meaningful omissions.
tasks.human_edge: The transcriptionist detects uncertainty and asks instead of inventing speech.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass typing with audio verification retained.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dragon Copilot supports medical dictation and documentation; this establishes drafting capability rather than local transcriptionist time savings.
The Dutch GP study found less documentation time while total consultation time did not change; its result is not a direct transcriptionist productivity estimate.
Model knowledge: the proposed typing and review shares are unmeasured transcription scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is transcription to a checked draft, excluding original dictation and the clinician's existing clinical approval. That approval is unchanged outside labour, not new transferred checking.

OTHER means clinical documentation system. The clinician supplies audio and encounter context under the existing process. In s1 the transcriptionist verifies patient/encounter ID, dictator, audio version, language, report type and template; all capture remains in the 10% share.

Audio-faithfulness correction is counted in s2. Separate difficult dictionary/reference investigation belongs to task 9415 only when actually needed, and a team roll-up must assign each correction once. Unsupported passages remain queries rather than accepted guesses.

Test native dictation first; existing recognition runtime earns no new saving. Eight extra focal hours count model-change checks, sampled audio audits and failed recognition, and 5 other-role hours count documentation-system access and template maintenance.
unknowns: Existing recognition use and actual audio quality
Local report types and sign-off workflow
research_questions: Does total transcription time fall after full audio checking, corrections and failed recognition?

incremental.description: Recognition changes, audio audits and additional failures
Documentation administrator template and access maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked draft, audio version, patient encounter, template and unresolved query list handed off in s3; changes void transcriptionist approval. This is not clinical sign-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=10+75*0.40+15=55; gross 45%, net 37% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers already assisted transcription with zero new gain through clear audio with 28 points of typing removed minus 8 upkeep. Source listening and final checks remain.

tasks.short: Resolve ambiguous or inconsistent medical terminology

steps.what: Distinguish homonyms and investigate inconsistent medical terms using authoritative references

tasks.design: The transcriptionist checks ambiguous terminology against source dictation in the documentation system {OTHER} and authoritative references in {DOCS}. Unresolved clinical meaning goes to the dictator for clarification.
tasks.previous_blocker: A plausible word can still be wrong for the clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable references improve access, but choosing the intended term remains judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguity that the audio and record cannot resolve.
tasks.human_edge: The transcriptionist recognises when evidence is insufficient.

reach.learn: Reference quality and clinical query boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: contextual homonym and terminology investigation remains human; a dictionary match alone cannot establish intended meaning.

assumptions: Boundary is difficult terminology investigation beyond routine audio-faithfulness checks in task 9413. Each correction is assigned once; abbreviation expansion belongs to task 9417.

OTHER means clinical documentation system. The transcriptionist identifies uncertain wording and selects references during s1; no structured correct-term label is assumed free. The clinician supplies clarification only where the existing query process requires it.
Test native reference search first; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new terminology model or reference process is added.
unknowns: Frequency of unresolved terms and available references
research_questions: Which ambiguities can references resolve without clinician clarification?

already_counted.description: Source listening, reference investigation and unresolved queries

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Difficult terminology judgement remains and routine transcription corrections are not counted again.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify medical reports and verify their filing destination and record identity
Set up record folders and populate medical file metadata
Check and save medical files and database changes

tasks.design: Configure native filing templates in the clinical record system {OTHER} to reuse verified metadata. The transcriptionist retains identity checks and approves each record save; missing identifiers remain a manual exception.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report metadata can be retyped while setting up folders and record entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native defaults and field reuse can repeat known filing structures without interpreting clinical content.
tasks.still_hard: Identity conflicts, duplicate reports and wrong-version documents.
tasks.human_edge: The transcriptionist checks whether the report belongs in the intended record.
tasks.altitude: Less metadata copying with filing accountability retained.

reach.learn: Patient identity resolution and record versioning

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native filing configuration can reuse verified metadata; the saving is unmeasured and does not remove identity checks.

assumptions: Boundary is file and database maintenance, excluding report transcription and clinical approval.

OTHER means clinical record system. Original report authors supply reports through existing processes. In s1 the transcriptionist verifies and captures patient/encounter ID, document ID and version, report type, author, dates, status, destination and access class; all capture remains in the 45% share.

Unmatched identities, absent fields or duplicate versions return to manual filing; no free structured match-confidence flag is assumed. Test native defaults first; existing automatic filing earns no new saving.
Seven extra focal hours count template changes and additional filing exceptions; 3 other-role hours count records administrator mapping and access maintenance.
unknowns: Current automatic filing and metadata completeness
research_questions: Can native field reuse prevent wrong-patient and duplicate-version filing after corrections?

already_counted.description: Identity checks and structured filing capture
Final filing checks and save approval

incremental.description: Template maintenance and additional filing exceptions
Records administrator mapping and access maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact filing entry, report version, patient encounter, destination and access class checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+25=70; gross 30%, net 23% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers existing automated filing with zero gain through 17 points of metadata copying removed minus 7 upkeep. Identity and final record checks remain.

tasks.short: Expand medical jargon and abbreviations accurately

steps.what: Translate medical jargon and abbreviations into context-appropriate expanded forms

loop.purpose: Propose contextual expansions for non-unique medical wording
loop.input: Selected source spans, relevant context and approved reference entries
loop.output: Proposed expansions with reference notes and ambiguity flags
loop.check: Transcriptionist checks that expanded meaning matches the source, clinical context and authorised terminology; alternative meanings remain unresolved
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass; ambiguous terms return to manual reference lookup or clinician query
loop.why_not_simpler: Native dictionaries handle unique expansions first; a fixed replacement cannot resolve terms with several clinical meanings

steps.what: Verify expanded forms and apply approved wording to the medical record draft

tasks.design: Use native terminology dictionaries in {OTHER} first, with a bounded contextual proposal only for wording that fixed lookup cannot resolve. The transcriptionist checks the intended meaning against references in {DOCS} and applies only supported expansions to the draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same abbreviation can have several clinical meanings.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound proposals can assist lookup while ambiguity remains a human decision.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing when the source does not support a unique expansion.
tasks.human_edge: The transcriptionist preserves uncertainty and asks the clinician rather than changing meaning silently.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass lookup with expansion responsibility retained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: contextual expansion proposals may reduce lookup time, but fixed dictionaries should handle unique cases and every ambiguous expansion needs checking.

assumptions: Boundary is abbreviation and jargon expansion, excluding general homonym research in task 9415. Each wording correction is counted once.

OTHER means clinical documentation system. Within retained s1 time the transcriptionist selects source spans and captures record version, contextual passage, approved reference edition and unresolved questions before requesting a proposal. The 52.5 retained hours include capture, lookup and semantic correction.

Missing context or conflicting reference meanings return to manual lookup or the existing clinician-query process. No structured intended-meaning label is supplied free; the tool does not approve clinical content.

Test native dictionaries first; existing automatic expansion earns no new saving. Six extra focal hours count reference/prompt changes, sampled expansion audits and failed proposals; no new checking is transferred to clinicians.
unknowns: Existing dictionary coverage and ambiguity frequency
research_questions: Does total expansion time fall after context capture, reference checks and failed proposals?

already_counted.description: Context capture, reference lookup and draft meaning checks

incremental.description: Reference changes, expansion audits and failed proposals

approvals.approved_version: Exact source report version, selected spans, contextual evidence and expanded wording checked in s2; changes void approval. Clinical report sign-off remains separate.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70*0.75+30=82.5; gross 17.5%, net 11.5% after 6 focal upkeep. Range covers unsuccessful contextual proposals with no gain through 11 points of lookup removed minus 6 upkeep. Final meaning checks remain.
